question: List the email addresses of customers who registered before 2024.
sql: SELECT email FROM customers WHERE created_at < '2024-01-01'

question: How many products have a stock greater than 50?
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE stock > 50

question: Show the name and price of the single cheapest product.
sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price ASC LIMIT 1

question: List the distinct payment methods that have been used.
For every payment, show the payment id and the status of the order it belongs to.
sql: SELECT pay.id, o.status FROM payments pay JOIN orders o ON o.id = pay.order_id

question: List the names of products that have received at least one review, without duplicates.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.name FROM products p JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.id

question: Which category names contain at least one product with zero stock?
sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.id WHERE p.stock = 0

question: List the names of customers who have no cancelled orders, including any customer who has placed no orders at all.
sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'cancelled')
notes: The trailing clause is deliberate: without it, an inner-join reading that silently drops order-less customers would be equally defensible.

question: What is the total amount across all refunded payments?
sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM payments WHERE status = 'refunded'

question: How many distinct customers have placed at least one order?
For each order status that has more than two orders, show the status and the average order total.
sql: SELECT status, AVG(total) FROM orders GROUP BY status HAVING COUNT(*) > 2

question: Show the category name and the total stock across its products, for categories whose total stock is above 50.
sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(p.stock) FROM categories c JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(p.stock) > 50

question: Show the id and the status for every payment.
notes: 'status' exists on both orders and payments. The question names payments.

question: For every order item, show the order id and the difference between the product's current price and the price actually paid for it.
sql: SELECT oi.order_id, p.price - oi.unit_price FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
notes: Requires distinguishing products.price (current) from order_items.unit_price (historical) in one expression.

question: List the names of the categories.
notes: 'name' exists on customers, products and categories; only one of them is asked for.

question: Show the id of every review that was created during 2024.
sql: SELECT id FROM reviews WHERE created_at >= '2024-01-01' AND created_at < '2025-01-01'
notes: 'created_at' exists on customers, products and reviews.
